info.title: Fundable API
info.description: Canonical OpenAPI specification for the Fundable API. This file bundles the Deals, Companies, Investors, People, Alerts, Location, and Industry endpoints.

post.summary: Search and filter funding rounds by company, investor, and round details
post.description:
Retrieve venture capital deals with advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 4 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific deals by UUID
- `deal` - Filter by deal attributes (financing type, size, date)
- `company` - Filter by company attributes (location, industry, size)
- `investors` - Filter by investor participation (firms or people, by UUID)

Retrieve detailed company information using any supported identifier format.
The API intelligently detects the identifier type and queries accordingly.

- `domain` - Company domain or full URL (e.g., "stripe.com" or "https://stripe.com")

- `crunchbase` - Crunchbase organization URL

post.summary: Search and filter companies with recent funding details
post.description:
Retrieve companies with advanced filtering, pagination, sorting, and optional AI-powered semantic search.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 4 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific companies by UUID, domain, LinkedIn, or Crunchbase
- `company` - Filter by company attributes (search, location, industry, size, etc.)
- `latest_deal` - Filter by latest funding round attributes (type, size, date, investors)
- `investors` - Filter by investors (firms or people) across all rounds

identifiers.description: Look up specific companies by identifier

search_query.description: AI-powered semantic search — a flexible replacement for an industry tag. Use it to target a niche industry or specific product type by describing what the company does — its product, technology, or business model (e.g. "AI-powered medical imaging diagnostics" or "vertical SaaS for dental practices"). Best for product/category targeting the fixed industry list can't capture. Do NOT use it for other attributes like stage, location, funding, or employee count — apply those with the dedicated filter fields instead. Results include a similarity score and are sorted by relevance.

min_relevance.description: Minimum similarity threshold (0-1). Only applies with search_query.

locations.description: Location permalinks. Use /location/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

industries.description: Industry permalinks. Use /industry/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

super_categories.description: Super category permalinks (automatically includes related industries). Use /industry/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

ipo_status.description: IPO status filter. Valid: public, private

financing_types.description: Financing types with optional modifiers (pre, extension)

created_start.description: Latest deal record added to the system on or after this date (ISO 8601). Filters by ingestion date (`created_at`), not the announcement date — useful for finding rounds newly added to Fundable.

created_end.description: Latest deal record added to the system on or before this date (ISO 8601). Filters by ingestion date (`created_at`), not the announcement date.

investor_ids.description: Filter by investors who participated in the latest deal only

investors.description: Filter by investors (firms or people) across all funding rounds

investor_ids.description: Investor UUIDs — matches companies where these investors participated in any round ever

people_ids.description:
Person UUIDs — matches companies where any of these people participated in any round
as an **angel investor** OR as a **lead partner** of an investing firm.
Resolve via `/people/{id}`.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Ignored when search_query is provided (sorted by relevance).

filter_only.summary: Filter by IPO status and industry

batch_lookup.summary: Look up specific companies by domain

total_count.description: Total number of companies matching the filter criteria

credits_used.description: Number of credits consumed by this request

credit_source.description: Source of credits used (only included for non-API tier keys)

monthly_credits_remaining.description: Remaining monthly credits (only included for non-API tier keys)

purchased_credits_remaining.description: Remaining purchased credits (only included for non-API tier keys)

Retry-After.description: Number of seconds to wait before retrying

post.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of investors with optional filtering.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 3 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific investors by UUID, domain, LinkedIn, or Crunchbase
- `investor` - Filter by investor entity attributes (location, employee count)
- `company_investments` - Filter by portfolio (industries, deal characteristics, etc.). Supports semantic search via `search_query` + `min_relevance`.

When `company_investments` filters are active, each investor in the response includes `filtered_deal_count` and `filtered_lead_count`.

locations.description: Investor HQ location permalinks. Use /location/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

company_investments.description: Portfolio filters (filter by companies the investor has invested in)

search_query.description:
AI-powered semantic search matched against each investor's
portfolio companies — a flexible replacement for an industry tag.
Use it to target a niche industry or specific product type by
describing what those companies do — their product, technology, or
business model (e.g. "climate-focused carbon capture hardware"). Do
NOT use it for other attributes like stage, location, or funding —
apply those with the dedicated `company_investments` and `investor`
filter fields instead. When provided, results are ranked by how
closely an investor's portfolio matches the query rather than the
default sort.

min_relevance.description:
Minimum relevance score threshold (0–1) for the portfolio-based
semantic search. Only applies when `search_query` is provided.
Investors whose portfolio match score falls below this threshold
are excluded. Defaults to 0 (return all results).

locations.description: Portfolio company location permalinks. Use /location/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

industries.description: Portfolio company industry permalinks. Use /industry/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

super_categories.description: Broad industry super-category permalinks. Use /industry/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

total_raised_min.description: Minimum total raised by portfolio companies (USD)

total_raised_max.description: Maximum total raised by portfolio companies (USD)

financing_types.description: Financing types with optional modifiers (pre, extension)

deal_start_date.description: Filter deals on or after this date (ISO 8601)

deal_end_date.description: Filter deals on or before this date (ISO 8601)

only_lead_deals.description: When true, only count deals where investor was lead

min_matching_deals.description: Minimum number of deals matching the portfolio filters

sort_by.description:
Sort order for results.
- **most_recent_deal** — Date of most recent investment (newest first)
- **recent_deals** — Deals in last 12 months (highest first)
- **deals_led_ltm** — Lead deals in last 12 months (highest first)
- **total_deals** — All-time deal count (highest first)
- **matching_deals** — Deals matching portfolio filters (highest first)

post.summary: Search people with cross-type filters and optional semantic search
post.description:
Retrieve people with advanced filtering, pagination, sorting, and optional AI-powered semantic search.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 4 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific people by UUID, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, or Twitter
- `person` - Filter by person attributes (role, contact info, job title, education, prior employers)
- `company` - Filter by current employer attributes (industry, location, funding, IPO status, etc.)
- `investor` - Filter by investor activity (firm, deal characteristics, portfolio companies)

person_type.description:
Restrict results to one population. `company` returns only people with a
current employer (founders, executives, employees). `investor` returns only
people who invest. `any` (default) returns the union — anyone matching the
other filter blocks regardless of population.

identifiers.description: Look up specific people by identifier

roles.description: Person's role at their current employer

contact_types.description: Available contact info on the person

linkedin_companies.description: Filter by previous/current employer LinkedIn company IDs

company.description: Current-employer attribute filters. Setting any field implicitly requires the person to have a current employer.

search_query.description: AI-powered semantic search against the person's current employer — a flexible replacement for an industry tag. Use it to target a niche industry or specific product type by describing what that company does — its product, technology, or business model (e.g. "climate tech carbon accounting software"). Do NOT use it for other attributes like stage, location, or funding — apply those with the dedicated filter fields instead. Overrides explicit sort_by — results are ordered by relevance.

min_relevance.description: Minimum similarity threshold (0-1). Only applies with search_query.

locations.description: Location permalinks. Use /location/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

industries.description: Industry permalinks. Use /industry/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

super_categories.description: Super category permalinks (auto-includes related industries). Use /industry/search to find permalinks. A value that is not an exact permalink is silently ignored (returns zero results, no error).

total_raised_min.description: Minimum total raised by current employer (USD)

total_raised_max.description: Maximum total raised by current employer (USD)

investor_people_ids.description:
Person UUIDs — filter to people whose current employer has ever raised
from any of these people as an **angel investor** OR as a **lead partner**
of an investing firm. Resolve via `/people/{id}`.

latest_deal.description: Nested. Filters on the current employer's most recent funding round.

financing_types.description: Financing types with optional modifiers (pre, extension)

investor_ids.description: Filter to deals where these investor UUIDs participated

investor_locations.description: Filter to deals with investors HQ'd in these locations

investor.description:
Filters on the investor entity (firm) and on the person's deal activity.
Setting any field (including any nested `deals.*` field) implicitly requires
the person to be an investor.

deals.description:
Nested. Combined deal-activity and portfolio-company filters. Includes:
deal-level controls (`investment_type`, `min_matching_deals`, `only_lead_deals`),
round-level filters (`financing_types`, `size_min/max`, `date_start/end`), and
portfolio-company attributes (`industries`, `super_categories`,
`portfolio_locations`, `portfolio_employee_count`, `ipo_status`,
`total_raised_min/max`, plus semantic `search_query` / `min_relevance`).

search_query.description: AI-powered semantic search against the person's portfolio companies — a flexible replacement for an industry tag. Use it to target a niche industry or specific product type by describing what those companies do — their product, technology, or business model (e.g. "AI infrastructure for model training"). Do NOT use it for other attributes like stage, location, or funding — apply those with the dedicated filter fields instead. Overrides explicit sort_by — results are ordered by relevance.

min_relevance.description: Minimum similarity threshold (0-1). Only applies with search_query.

investment_type.description: Filter by whether the person invests as an angel, under a firm, or both

only_lead_deals.description: Only count deals where the person/firm was a lead investor

min_matching_deals.description: Require at least this many deals to match the deal filters

financing_types.description: Financing types for the person's investment activity

size_min.description: Minimum deal size (USD) for the person's deal activity

size_max.description: Maximum deal size (USD) for the person's deal activity

total_raised_min.description: Minimum total raised by the portfolio company (USD)

total_raised_max.description: Maximum total raised by the portfolio company (USD)

sort_by.description:
Sort order. All values are universally accepted — non-applicable values (e.g. `lead_deal_count`
when no investor filter is set) resolve to 0 / null via COALESCE and naturally sort to the bottom (DESC).
Ignored when `company.search_query` or `investor.deals.search_query` is set (results are then
ordered by semantic relevance).

batch_lookup.summary: Look up specific people by LinkedIn URL

angel_investors_active_2024.summary: People who made at least 3 angel investments in 2024

message.description: Optional friendly message (e.g. "No people found matching your filters" when empty)

total_count.description: Total number of people matching the filter criteria

credits_used.description: Number of credits consumed by this request

credit_source.description: Source of credits used (only included for non-API tier keys)

monthly_credits_remaining.description: Remaining monthly credits (only included for non-API tier keys)

purchased_credits_remaining.description: Remaining purchased credits (only included for non-API tier keys)

400.description: Validation error (invalid types, dates, enums, or empty `search_query`)

429.description:
Two distinct cases share this status:
- `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — per-minute API rate limit
- `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — semantic-search monthly usage limit (only when `company.search_query` or `investor.deals.search_query` was set)

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (sent for `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` only)

504.description: Semantic search timed out (only when `company.search_query` or `investor.deals.search_query` was set)

get.summary: Search for a person by name or identifier
get.description:
Look up people using one of five search methods. Exactly one parameter must be provided.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search across both investors AND non-investor people (founders, employees). Returns up to 10 results.
- `id` — Person UUID lookup (returns 0 or 1)
- `linkedin` — LinkedIn person URL or slug
- `crunchbase` — Crunchbase person URL or slug
- `twitter` — Twitter/X URL or handle

`person_type` on each result indicates which pool the row came from
(`investor` wins when a person is in both). For full person detail, use `/person`.

parameters.name: person_type
parameters.description:
Optional filter restricting results to one pool. `investor` keeps only
people tracked as investors/angels; `company` keeps only non-investor
people (founders, CEOs, employees). Omit to search both. Applies to
both name and identifier modes — identifier lookups return empty if
the resolved person doesn't match the requested type.

person_type.description: Which pool the result came from. Mirrors the request-body discriminator on POST /people.

Retry-After.description: Number of seconds to wait before retrying

get.description:
Retrieve saved alert data including all deals that matched the alert criteria within the specified date range.
Results include a flattened array of deals sorted by date (newest first) with duplicates removed.

**Multiple Alerts Support:**
- Query multiple alerts in a single request (up to 10)
- Each alert returns its own flattened deals array
- Different alerts can have different frequencies (e.g., one daily, one weekly)
- Total deal count across all alerts determines credit usage

**Important Notes:**
- All alert_ids must belong to alerts you have access to
- Deals are flattened from all time periods and sorted by date DESC (newest first)
- Duplicate deals are automatically removed
- Each deal includes AI-generated reasoning for why it matched the alert criteria
- Deal structure is simplified with flattened company information for easier integration

parameters.name: alert_ids
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of alert UUIDs (up to 10 alerts per request).
All alerts must be associated with your API key's account.
Example: "uuid1,uuid2,uuid3"

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description:
Start date for the alert data range (ISO 8601 format).
Results will include deals from this date onwards.

get.summary: Get alert configurations for authenticated user
get.description:
Retrieve all alert configurations for the authenticated user (identified by API key).
Returns configuration metadata including filters, frequency, and descriptions.

**Important Notes:**
- This endpoint does NOT consume usage credits (actualUsageCount: 0)
- Returns only configuration metadata, not deal data
- Does not require any query parameters - user is identified by API key
- All configurations for the authenticated user are returned (no pagination)

**Authentication:**
- User identity is automatically determined from the API key
- No email or user_id parameter needed

**Use Cases:**
- Look up what alerts are configured for the authenticated user
- Retrieve alert filter settings for external integrations
- Audit alert configurations programmatically

get.summary: Search locations by name and optionally filter by type
get.description:
Look up locations (cities, states, countries, regions) by name with fuzzy matching. The `name` parameter is required; `type` is optional.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search with relevance scoring (required)
- `type` — Optional filter by location type: `CITY`, `STATE`, `REGION`, or `COUNTRY`
- `location_type` — Alias for `type`

Examples:
- `?name=san francisco`
